title: Portable SDK contracts for incremental output, tool choreography, and typed adapters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a portable SDK contract that standardizes progressive (streaming) model output events, tool/function invocation choreography, and typed adapter helpers across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. The contract should enable: (1) incremental JSON event emission for structured outputs, (2) a deterministic handshake for tool calls (call/request/response/error) that works across sync and async runtimes, and (3) typed validation helpers to convert runtime events into language-native typed objects with backwards-compatible fallbacks.

Motivation: Current language SDKs have divergent streaming ergonomics and tooling-call wiring. This causes confusing patterns in downstream applications when using progressive responses + tool calls + typed outputs together (examples: partial JSON emission, interleaved tool request while streaming, and backpressure/closure conventions). We need a single conceptual contract and small shim libraries so apps can write one integration pattern and expect similar behavior across TS/Python/Go.

Non-goals: Replacing all existing SDK APIs; this is an opt-in compatibility layer and example set. We will not implement runtime server changes beyond minimal compatibility headers and event names.

High-level approach:
- Define an event vocabulary (event_type, seq, payload, schema_uri, provenance) that maps to streaming chunks. Keep event frames small and JSON-first to maximize compatibility with existing HTTP/WS/SSE transports.
- Tool choreography: define explicit events: tool_call_request, tool_call_response, tool_call_error, tool_call_close. Each event includes an id so the client can correlate. The runtime must support interleaving tool events with subsequent token/event frames.
- Typed adapters: publish lightweight language helpers that accept event streams and produce: (a) an async iterator of typed Message objects for JS/Python, (b) a channel/reader pattern for Go, plus validators using JSON Schema (fallback to permissive parsing if schema not available).
- Example apps: small reference implementations (chat-with-tool, streaming-json-forms, progressive-embedder) in each language demonstrating patterns and migration guidance.

API contract (informal):
- Common event envelope: {"type": "<string>", "id": "<string>", "seq": <int>, "payload": <object|string>, "schema": "<uri>|null", "final": true|false }
- Event types: model_token, structured_chunk, tool_call_request, tool_call_response, tool_call_error, control_ping, control_snapshot

Deliverables:
- RFC doc (Confluence) with examples and migration notes.
- TS/Python/Go adapter libs (small, <= 200 SLOC each) published under redwood-sdk/adapters.
- Example apps and unit/integration tests.
- One migration guide and a console doc recording telemetry events to monitor adoption.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Adapter libs expose a clearly documented API for consuming progressive events in each language and pass the provided conformance test harness.
2) Tool choreography test harness validates correct correlation of request/response/error and supports interleaving with streaming tokens.
3) At least three example apps (chat-with-tool, streaming-json-form, progressive-embedder) compile and run in CI for each language.
4) Migration guide and RFC reviewed and approved by PM (Ravi Kapoor) and Design (Maya Rivera).
5) No breaking changes to existing default SDK behavior; clients opt-in via a feature flag header or SDK opt-in constructor.
6) Integration tests validate fallback parsing when schema URI is absent.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions so far:
- Use JSON event envelope to avoid introducing binary framing. This maximizes compatibility with HTTP chunking and SSE.
- Choose 'id' as UUID v4 strings for correlation; 'seq' is monotonic per-id.
- Schema URIs point to versioned JSON Schema hosted under https://schemas.redwood.ai/sdk-events/. If unreachable, adapters fall back to lenient parsing with a logged warning.
- For TypeScript: provide both a stream async iterator (for fetch/streams) and a Node EventEmitter wrapper. For Python: provide an async generator (async for) and a synchronous iterator that does cooperative blocking reads. For Go: provide a Reader-like interface exposing NextEvent() and a channel helper for goroutines.
- Backpressure: adapters should expose a pause/resume signal for stream sources that support it; otherwise buffer up to 64 events by default and expose a maxBuffer config.

Notes on tooling choreography:
- tool_call_request payload includes: {"tool": "<string>", "input": <object>, "id": "<string>"}. Runtime forwards this to the tool runner and emits tool_call_response with same id. Errors use tool_call_error and include canonical error_code and message.
- If model issues repeated tool_call_request for same id, adapters should de-duplicate by default (configurable).

Security and performance:
- Adapters must sanitize tool payloads before writing to logs.
- Keep adapters zero-copy when possible; avoid heavyweight JSON+schema reserialization on hot paths.

Compatibility/migration:
- Default SDK constructors unchanged. New adapters are surfaced as 'compat' modules and opt-in via: new RedwoodClient({compat: {eventAdapter: true}}) or RedwoodClient.with_compat() in Python/Go.
- Provide a console telemetry event category: sdk.compat.adapter.v1 to monitor adoption and errors.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Initial spike: prototype TS adapter that converts SSE events into async iterator. Found ambiguity in how tool_call_request correlation should be represented when multiple tool calls are pending. Proposed adding explicit 'id' and 'seq' fields. - Asha
2026-02-28 - Design review with PM/Design: agreed on JSON-first envelope and schema URIs, asked to add a 'provenance' optional field to aid debugging (runtime/model/tool). Action: update RFC. - Maya
2026-03-03 - Engineering sync: Lila explored Go patterns. Decided to expose both blocking NextEvent() and non-blocking channel versions to match idiomatic Go. Added maxBuffer config. - Lila

2026-03-07 - PR feedback (TS): request to include small ergonomic helper to rehydrate typed objects from schema-less payloads (e.g., permissiveParsed<T>(obj)). Also add example for streaming partial JSON objects safely. - Code review by Tomasz
2026-03-10 - Security review request opened for sanitization rules and logging policy. Security owners: Priya Shah. Outcome: require adapters to take a 'sanitizeLogs' flag and default to true. - Lila

2026-03-14 - Integration test added validating interleaved tool events with streaming tokens. Current status: tests pass for TS, failing intermittently for Go due to race on de-dup buffer. Investigating. - Lila
